headline: Single-cell and spatial profiling maps immune and tumor cell states across diseases
label: Single Cell Immune Transcriptomics
summary: Recent papers extend single-cell and spatial transcriptomics from cell-type description toward state distributions and niche organization linked to therapy.
synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell and spatial resolution of immune and stromal cell states in diseased tissue, with several studies relating these states to clinical or therapeutic outcomes. Spatial transcriptomics defines immunological niches in atopic dermatitis, and spatiotemporal mapping of tertiary lymphoid structures in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is tied to clinical outcomes. Single-cell and spatial profiling of Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia resolves immune and structural cell coordination across time, and a single-cell immune atlas extends this to bacterial pneumonia. A mechanistic AP-1 model calibrated to single-cell melanoma protein data links AP-1 state distributions to MAPK signaling. Other items, including glycolytic heterogeneity in colorectal cancer, NCACC spatial niche mapping in liver cancer, and a 1M-cell blood atlas, extend the same framing across malignancy and healthy tissue. The new element is a shift from describing populations toward explaining state distributions and niche organization in relation to therapy.
